title: assert vs precondition vs fatalError
hints: `precondition` stops the program in all builds; validate user input with normal code instead.
Filter out negative ages **before** calling `validatedAge`, then add a summary line.
jsBridge: `assert` checks only in debug builds, `precondition` checks in release too, and `fatalError` always crashes. In JS, `console.assert` only logs. Swift's assertions actually stop the program, which is the point.

compass.q: `console.assert` doesn't stop execution. Why are Swift's assertions designed to crash?
